subject: Performance targets recap and pilot plan (PulseIQ)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@pulseiq.com>, Rex Park <rex.park@pulseiq.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance targets recap and pilot plan (PulseIQ)

Hi Maya / Rex —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick written recap so we’re aligned on the performance acceptance criteria and immediate next steps for the pilot: 

Summary of targets you confirmed on the call:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 350 ms for payloads ~512 tokens (text-gen use case).
- First-byte / streaming: first fragment delivered < 120 ms for streaming UI (progressive output required).
- Throughput / concurrency: sustained 150 concurrent requests (avg QPS target ~125), with short bursts to 300 QPS during peak traffic.
- Availability: 99.9% during business hours, automatic fallback to smaller model if latency exceeds threshold.

What we’ll provide this week (attachments):
- pulseiq_slo_checklist_v1.csv (detailed acceptance items + measurement hooks)
- demo_trace_20270914.json (server-side trace from today’s demo)
- mutual_action_plan_pulseiq_v1.docx (timeline + PO/contract milestones)

Asks / clarification items for PulseIQ:
1) Can you confirm the payload distribution? We assume ~60% short queries (<64 tokens), 30% medium (65-512), 10% long (>512). If that’s off, tell us so we can tune batching/cache.
2) Is the p95 requirement firm for all endpoints, or only for the primary customer-facing route?
3) Do you expect encrypted on-prem logs (HSM/KMS) as part of the pilot? If so, we’ll include that in the Dedicated trial quote.

Next steps (proposed):
- Friday 9/17: internal kickoff between PulseIQ engineering + Redwood SEs to validate trace-level requirements and test dataset.
- Week of 9/20: 2-week reserved-capacity pilot (dedicated pool) to validate SLOs under representative load.
- Following pilot: performance acceptance sign-off and PO for Q4 reserved capacity if targets are met.

If that matches your expectations I’ll book the kickoff — please indicate preferred times for Fri 9/17.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

(attachments: pulseiq_slo_checklist_v1.csv; demo_trace_20270914.json; mutual_action_plan_pulseiq_v1.docx)

From: Maya Singh <maya@pulseiq.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rex Park <rex.park@pulseiq.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance targets recap and pilot plan (PulseIQ)

Thanks Soojin — great summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the trace: 

- Concurrency: we’ll bump sustained target to 200 concurrent requests (avg QPS ~165) and still expect bursts to 350 for brief windows. The higher sustained concurrency is because we fan-out reads across multiple user sessions.
- Streaming: we need the first fragment for streaming UI to be <100 ms (we can accept up to 120 ms as a soft limit but prefer 100 ms). Also want cursored partials for very long responses.
- p95: this p95 target applies to the primary customer-facing endpoint only. Internal admin endpoints can be relaxed to p95 <= 700 ms.
- Security: yes, KMS-backed encryption for logs is required during pilot; we can provide our key.

We’re available for the kickoff Fri 9/17 — prefer 10:00–11:30 PT.

One more question: what fallback model do you propose if our primary model exceeds latency threshold? Is there an auto-failover to a quantized variant you recommend?

Best,
Maya

--
Maya Singh
Head of Product, PulseIQ
maya@pulseiq.com | +1 (212) 555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance targets recap and pilot plan (PulseIQ)

Internal notes for kickoff / SE playbook: 

- Demo trace (attached) shows spikes in KV cache misses at ~120ms which will push p95; recommend enabling prefix/KV caching aggressively for the primary route and prewarm caches during load tests.
- For sustained 200 concurrency with bursts to 350 we should propose a Dedicated pool sized for 8 x A100-equivalent slots (TBD after load run). Quantized 4-bit variant works as fallback for <10% quality degradation but reduces memory footprint ~2.3x — good candidate for automatic fallback.
- Streaming first-fragment <100 ms: we can hit this with continuous batching disabled for the first token and a small micro-batch for subsequent tokens. Need to instrument client tolerances for partials.
- KMS log encryption: supported, but latency for log writes can increase tail by ~5–8 ms; include this in acceptance gating.

Attachments: inference_notes_pulseiq.txt (excerpted profiler notes), demo_trace_20270914.json (from Soojin)

Action items for Friday kickoff:
1) Validate sample payload distribution (Soojin)
2) Confirm key exchange for KMS (PulseIQ)
3) Run baseline load script (Marcus + PulseIQ eng) to capture traces for sizing

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance targets recap and pilot plan (PulseIQ)

Maya — thanks for the fast response and the updated numbers. Confirming the adjusted targets and next steps: 

- Confirmed SLOs: p95 <= 350 ms (primary), first-fragment streaming <= 100 ms (hard preference), sustained concurrency 200, burst 350. Admin endpoints p95 <= 700 ms.
- KMS: we’ll accept your provided key for the pilot; Marcus will include the encryption latency in the gates.
- Fallback plan: automatic failover to quantized 4-bit variant (recommended by Marcus) with canary ratio 10%→50% while monitoring quality regressions in the eval set.

Kickoff booked for Fri 9/17 10:30 PT (30–60 min) — invite sent.
Pilot logistics / asks of PulseIQ:
- Provide sample payload distribution (JSON) and API keys for test harness by EOD Mon 9/20.
- PO or formal approval to proceed with reserved-capacity pilot by 9/24 to meet Q4 timelines (we’ve included the timeline in the attached mutual_action_plan_pulseiq_v1.docx).

I’ll circulate a short agenda + shared drive with runbook and load scripts ahead of the kickoff. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Soojin
